final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed its position to match the existing audit concern: operational readiness and reversibility may support a monitored release posture, but they do not satisfy the policy condition for certification while the affected segment remains exposed and there is no approved risk acceptance or exclusion control. That is a reframing of the same record, not new evidence. Because the missing approval/disclosure predicate is an unresolved compliance condition rather than a caveat on an otherwise satisfied standard, the proper final verdict remains noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: Policy requires either exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance covering the exposure before rollout monitoring can mitigate the weakness.
The small-business onboarding segment remains below target on long-context onboarding support and remains exposed in the randomized 6% rollout.
The risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and does not mention the exposed small-business onboarding segment.
No final disclosure artifact is in evidence showing the material limitation was disclosed before launch.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the disclosure and approval predicates in the policy.
